memory_lessons.applicability: Softmax workloads using the same CUDA benchmark and one-row-per-CTA mapping; the result does not establish repeatability or isolate fusion from configuration effects.
memory_lessons.claim: The earlier adaptive-warp fused candidate passed all eight supplied cases and measured 42.15 µs versus the 211.98 µs baseline. That comparison supports retaining the fused design as a candidate, but does not establish which individual transformation caused the difference.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the fixed-four-warps candidate against the adaptive-warp result, especially on short and 4096-element rows.

proposal.hypothesis: The previous correctness-valid one-row kernel measured 42.15 µs using 1/4/8 warps by row width. This candidate keeps the same fused row mapping and tests fixed four-warps CTAs for every width; reducing warps for 4096-element rows might help, while small rows may lose. No speedup is assumed before measurement.

retained: Replace the CUDA 2D floating-point no-gradient operation chain with one Triton program/CTA per complete row, preserving the stable max-subtract-exp-sum normalization.
Pad each row to the next power of two and use masks for tail loads and stores; accumulate in FP32 except for FP64 input.
Use a fixed four-warps launch for all row widths as a configuration contrast to the prior adaptive 1/4/8-warps candidate.
Pass input and output strides through the kernel, preserve output dtype and layout, and retain the PyTorch path for unsupported cases.
